description: Waffle chart: present-day structural vegetation of Australia (Atlas of Australian Resources, 1990, via ANBG), in 7 broad groups. 1,000 squares; each square is 0.1% of Australia (about 7,700 sq km). Each group's squares are calculated from its total area (largest-remainder rounding so they add to exactly 1,000), so the squares match the group shares shown in the legend. Hover over a square for the group's area, share, square count and the vegetation types it includes.

subtitle: Present-day vegetation by structural type. Each square = 0.1% of Australia (about 7,700 sq km).
Woodlands and shrublands cover more than three-quarters of the continent; forests cover about 5%.
